Ranked 5s Ends September 6: What’s Left, What You Can Still Earn, and How to Actually Queue

1 week ago
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:36
Instaread
Ranked 5s finishes on September 6, and because it only runs on weekend evenings, there's far less time left than the date suggests. I counted the sessions. It's one weekend. Here's what you can still realistically earn.

Ranked 5s — the full-premade competitive queue with its own ladder — ends on September 6, 2026.

That sounds like a week away. It isn’t, and this is the part that’s going to catch people out: Ranked 5s only runs on weekend evenings. Friday through Sunday, 8:00pm to 1:00am, and nothing outside that.

So let’s count what’s actually left.

You have one weekend. Three sessions. Fifteen hours.

Today is Monday, September 1st is tomorrow, and the mode closes on the 6th. Here’s every remaining window:

That’s it. Fifteen hours of queue availability, ever.

One useful simplification: every region runs on the same clock in local time. NA, EUW, EUNE, LAN, LAS, BR, OCE, SEA, KR, JP, TW, VN, TR — all of them are 8:00pm to 1:00am in their own shard’s timezone. There’s no conversion to do. Whatever 8pm means where you play, that’s when it opens.

One ambiguity worth planning around: Riot lists the end date as September 6, but the Sunday session runs past midnight into the 7th. Riot hasn’t clarified whether that final session runs in full. Treat Friday and Saturday as your guaranteed sessions and consider Sunday a bonus. Don’t build your plan around the last night.

Can you still get the rewards?

There are two, and the gap between them is enormous.

Rewards are based on the highest tier you achieved during the mode’s run, so nothing you’ve already earned can slip away.

The Icon has no listed criteria. If you’re going to play at all, you’re getting this.

The Banner needs Gold, and here’s the constraint that decides it: your team must play 5 placement matches before you have a tier and division at all. Only after those do you start climbing on Ranked 5s’ own bespoke MMR and LP ladder.

Do the arithmetic. Ranked 5s uses Tournament Draft — 3 bans, 3 picks, 2 bans, 2 picks — which adds five or six minutes of pick-and-ban before every game. Add queue time and a typical game length and you’re looking at roughly 40–45 minutes per cycle. Five placements is about three and a half hours. A single five-hour session can just about cover it, but only if you start at 8pm sharp with all five people already there.

So the honest verdict:

  • Haven’t placed yet? Friday night is your placement night. Whatever tier those five games land you in is realistically where you finish. If your team’s other-mode MMR is decent, Gold is possible directly out of placements — Riot uses your Ranked and Swiftplay MMR to seed those provisional matches.
  • Already placed and sitting below Gold? Saturday and Sunday are your climb, and it’s tight but real.
  • Already Gold or above? You’re done. The banner is yours. Play for fun.

Why you can’t queue right now

This is the single most common confusion with this mode, and it has three separate causes:

  1. It’s not a weekend evening. Outside Friday–Sunday 8pm–1am, the queue simply doesn’t exist.
  2. You don’t have five people. Ranked 5s is a full premade queue only. You can create a lobby alone, but you cannot enter matchmaking without a complete team of five. There is no solo queue version and Riot has been explicit that there won’t be — the whole point is coordinated play.
  3. You’re looking in the wrong place. It’s its own queue with its own ladder, separate from Solo/Duo and Flex.

Riot’s stated reason for the weekend-only window is queue health: the mode needs prep work, and restricting availability guarantees faster matchmaking instead of five people sitting in a lobby at 2pm on a Tuesday.

Good news on team-building: there are no tier restrictions. You can bring anyone from Unranked to Challenger onto the same team. If you’re short a player on Friday, you don’t need to find someone in your rank — you need to find someone who’ll show up.

The trap: what Ranked 5s does and doesn’t count for

Read this before you spend your last weekend on it.

Ranked 5s does NOT progress your ranked objectives. It runs its own season, overlapping the standard Solo/Flex seasons. You cannot earn the season’s Victorious skin or other ranked rewards through Ranked 5s. Those come only from Solo/Duo or Flex.

Ranked 5s DOES contribute to Battle Pass objectives and earns Battle Pass XP. So your weekend isn’t wasted on the Season 3: Act I pass front — those games feed the same track your Solo queue games do, and that pass runs to October 5.

Also worth knowing: there’s no decay. Because availability is limited, Riot disabled the decay penalty entirely. Missing sessions costs you nothing beyond the missed games.

Your pre-Friday checklist

If you want the banner, the work happens before 8pm on Friday, not during it.

  1. Lock in five people now. Not “probably five.” Five confirmed humans with the evening free. This is the single most common reason teams don’t place.
  2. Get into voice. Riot built this queue around direct communication and drafted the rules to assume it.
  3. Agree your draft plan in advance. Tournament Draft’s 3-3-2-2 structure is not the pick order your team is used to from Solo queue. Ten minutes of “who’s first pick, what are our three bans” on Thursday saves you a wasted game on Friday.
  4. Start at 8:00pm, not 8:40. With three and a half hours of placements to fit into a five-hour window, forty minutes of “waiting for Dave” is the difference between placing and not.
  5. Decide your fifth-player fallback. Someone will drop. Have a name ready.

Will Ranked 5s come back?

Riot hasn’t announced anything. But the structure here is different from a typical event mode — Ranked 5s has its own ladder, its own MMR system, its own reward track and its own season that deliberately overlaps the main ones. That’s a lot of infrastructure to build for a single ten-week run.

For context on how these calls usually go, we’ve tracked every limited-time League mode and which ones returned — the short version is that modes reusing existing systems come back cheaply and often, while bespoke ones live or die on engagement.

Ranked 5s sits awkwardly between the two. My read: a return in some form is more likely than not, but on Riot’s schedule and probably not soon. Don’t skip this weekend on the assumption it’ll be back in October.

FAQ

When exactly does Ranked 5s end? September 6, 2026. It started June 26.

What are the Ranked 5s hours? Friday to Sunday, 8:00pm to 1:00am, in your shard’s local time. Every region uses the same window.

Can I play Ranked 5s solo? No. It’s a full premade queue — you need all five players to enter matchmaking.

How many games do I need to get a rank? Five placement matches. Your opponents during those are seeded using your MMR from Ranked and Swiftplay.

What rewards can I get? An icon with no listed criteria, and a banner for reaching Gold tier or higher. Rewards are based on your highest tier achieved.

Does Ranked 5s count toward the Victorious skin? No. Only Solo/Duo and Flex matches count toward season ranked rewards.

Does it give Battle Pass XP? Yes. Ranked 5s games contribute to Battle Pass objectives and earn BXP normally.

Can I team with players from other tiers? Yes. There are no tier restrictions — Unranked through Challenger can play together.

Fifteen hours left, and most of what decides your outcome happens before Friday evening starts. Get your five confirmed, agree a draft plan, and be in the lobby at 8pm.

If you’re short a player, now’s the time to ask — with no tier restrictions, literally anyone counts.
